title: How to Create, Read, Update & Delete users in ASP.NET Core Identity
description: Perform CRUD operations on users with ASP.NET Core Identity.

data.text: In this tutorial we will perform **ASP.NET Core Identity CRUD Operations** — Creating, Reading, Updating, and Deleting users. These operations are the backbone of any user management system. Before continuing, make sure you have already [Setup and Configure ASP.NET Core Identity](/courses/aspnet-core/authentication-identity/setup-configure-aspnet-core-identity) in your app.

terms.definition: The central class in ASP.NET Core Identity for managing users. Provides methods like CreateAsync, FindByIdAsync, UpdateAsync, and DeleteAsync.
Your custom user class that inherits from IdentityUser. Represents a user record stored in the AspNetUsers table.
Returned by every Identity operation. Its Succeeded property tells you if the operation passed; Errors contains any failure details.
Hashes plain-text passwords before storing them. Identity never saves passwords in plain text.

data.text: **ASP.NET Core Identity UserManager<T>** lives in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity namespace and is the primary API for managing users. The generic parameter T is the class you use to represent users — in our case, AppUser.

rows: Returns all users stored in the Identity database as an IQueryable<AppUser>.
Finds a single user by their unique Id.
Registers a new user with the supplied password.
Persists changes made to an existing user.
Removes the user from the database.
Assigns the user to a named role.
Returns true if the user belongs to the specified role.

data.text: Updating a password requires hashing it first. Inject IPasswordHasher<AppUser> into the controller. Its HashPassword() method converts the plain-text password into the same hashed format Identity stores internally.

data.title: Exercise: Build a User Admin Page
data.description: Create a complete user management page with Create, Read, Update, and Delete functionality using ASP.NET Core Identity.
steps: Create the User.cs input model with Name, Email, and Password properties.
Add AdminController with Index (GET), Create (GET+POST), Update (GET+POST), and Delete (POST) actions.
Inject UserManager<AppUser> and IPasswordHasher<AppUser> into the controller.
Create Razor views for Index, Create, and Update.
Run the app at /Admin and register at least two users.
data.expectedOutcome: You can list all users, create new ones, edit their email/password, and delete them. All data is persisted in the AspNetUsers table.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: UserManager<AppUser> provides all CRUD methods for Identity users.
IdentityResult always wraps the outcome of an Identity operation.
Passwords must be hashed via IPasswordHasher before being stored.
The AspNetUsers table stores all user records; passwords are never kept in plain text.
data.takeaway: You now have a working user administration page. Next, learn how to enforce username, email, and password rules.
